static_traits.name: Chen Jing
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no psychotherapy or psychiatric treatment history; has not yet had similar psychological problems before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, coherent thinking; able to describe thoughts and feelings in skateboarding situations concretely; harsh self-evaluation, negative tone; frequent absolutist statements (e.g. 'I will never get better'); good cooperation with the counselor, willing to try recording small successes; tending to compare with others

basic_info.main_problem: I feel terrible at skateboarding, with no progress in years, which leaves me frustrated and self-doubting.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because this sense of self-doubt affects my enjoyment of skateboarding and causes distress.
growth_experiences: Took up skateboarding as a hobby years ago; despite regular practice and watching tutorials, long frustrated on certain tricks and moves; every time skating, especially seeing others complete moves with ease, self-doubt and frustration arise; after comparing progress speed with other skaters, formed self-labels of 'I am terrible' 'I will never get better'; has friends to chat with, but unwilling to express own inadequacy to them, leaving the long-term self-denial without interpersonal support and correction.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough / I am terrible
I lack the ability to learn skateboarding

special_situations.event: Seeing others complete moves with ease while skating
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I can't complete moves as smoothly as them, it means I am no good
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubling practice and watching tutorials; avoiding discussing my inadequacy with friends to reduce embarrassment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them; I am terrible

special_situations.event: Still unable to master certain tricks and moves after long practice
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I still can't learn certain tricks after years, it proves I'll never learn them
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Considering giving up skateboarding to avoid persistent failure

special_situations.event: Despite regular practice and watching tutorials, the number of failures is still relatively high
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If effort hasn't brought obvious progress immediately, my effort is meaningless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focuses only on failures; ignores small successes and progress
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These small successes don't count; they are too insignificant

special_situations.event: Comparing progress speed with other skaters
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my progress is slower than others', it means something is wrong with me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Continuous self-judgment and labeling ('I am terrible')
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: There must be something wrong with me

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized and to prove one's ability, able to enjoy the fun and vitality of skateboarding
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure and appearing 'inferior' after comparison, worrying about being negated and seen as 'problematic'
defense_goal: Avoiding exposing inadequacy to friends to reduce shame and the sense of being judged
Focusing attention on technique and practice details to lower exposure of vulnerable emotions (intellectualization tendency)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites attention to and acknowledgment of small successes, suggesting different perspectives on progress
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to believe small successes are unimportant and cannot represent real progress
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gentle tone validating their feelings, avoiding confrontation; inviting concrete examples and quantification of 'small successes', using open-ended questions and reflective listening, helping separate facts from evaluation.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked whether willing to discuss own inadequacy with friends or seek support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing expressing inadequacy will make me more embarrassed or not understood, hence choosing not to share
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Maintaining empathy and safety, using low-risk sharing invitations (e.g. describing only one concrete situation), and offering choice; encouraging identification and naming of emotions and their intensity, gradually increasing emotional capacity.

manifestations: Having friends to chat with about Average topics, but unwilling to discuss own inadequacy and vulnerability
Inner isolation and self-denial from self-comparison
When effort hasn't yet brought marked progress, tending to see practice as 'meaningless'
The fun of the interest eroded by self-denial and comparison
outcomes: Has a negative impact on the emotions and motivation of daily life

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequent self-critical statements (e.g. 'I am terrible' 'I will never get better')
Comparing with others and negating own progress
Unwilling to discuss own sense of inadequacy with friends

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Considers giving up skateboarding, bears the disappointment and pressure inwardly
Still choosing not to seek emotional support despite having friends

exception_events.target_problem: When practicing skateboarding and seeing others complete moves with ease, the client typically engages in self-denial, low mood, and considers quitting.
exception_events.unique_outcome: The client mentions 'sometimes I can successfully land a certain move', and in those practices small progress and success appeared.
exception_events.reason: Different approach: sustained regular practice and watching tutorials, gradually accumulating move essentials, thus occasionally landing successfully.

positive_force: Willing to accept counseling, try recording small successes, and cognitive reframing
Occasionally has small successes (proving progress is possible)
Having basic social support (friends to chat with about Average topics)
negative_force: Black-and-white thinking, overgeneralization, mental filtering, disqualifying the positive and other cognitive distortions
Unwilling to discuss inadequacy with friends, limited access to emotional support
Low mood and decreased motivation, affecting daily life and interest experience

target_behavior.behavior: Self-denial and comparison in skateboarding situations (accompanied by statements like 'I am terrible' 'I will never get better'), leading to low mood and decreased motivation
antecedent: Seeing others complete moves with ease
Repeatedly failing at specific techniques and moves
target_behavior.core_reason: Long comparing progress speed with others, and forming black-and-white, overgeneralizing, mental-filtering, and disqualifying-the-positive cognitive distortions after failures
target_behavior.function: Escaping the shame and discomfort of failure, trying to gain control through self-criticism or find reasons to quit
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced sense of enjoyment, low mood, insufficient motivation, even considering giving up skateboarding, affecting daily mood and energy
